objectives.text: Hold power and close the 2025 protest wave. The electoral commission declared Samia Suluhu Hassan the winner with 97.66% on 1 November 2025, after the main opposition party Chadema was disqualified (12 April 2025) and its leader Tundu Lissu was charged with treason. Samia called the unrest an attempted coup and defended the security forces. Two claims on the dead, not one number: the opposition says about 2,000 (CNN, 5 Nov 2025), the UN and rights groups say hundreds (OPB, Dec 2025); the government has published no toll.

objectives.text: Make Dar es Salaam the transit port of the region and take Uganda and DRC cargo from Mombasa. grand_strategy.reading: Samia Suluhu Hassan's government has answered the 2025 election protests with the security forces and a tighter grip on the opposition, and has paid for it with the Western money that its own ports and railways need. It is building a transit state: Dar es Salaam takes the Uganda and DRC cargo, and the concessions to DP World and CCECC tie the infrastructure to Gulf and Chinese capital, which it can take in place of the aid. The test is whether that capital can replace the Western aid lost since 2025 without the price in legitimacy and in the East African trade that the same policy strains, and whether a regional military role is possible again once the SADC mission has gone.

stances.note: Reluctant partner, cooling: our reading (confidence C), no source uses the word. Tanzania stays in the East African Community and the bilateral trade talks but resists the common-market commitments. The Regional Monitoring Committee blames it for 39% of EAC trade barriers; Kenya objected in July 2025 to a Tanzanian law on non-citizens and to price rises of up to 65% on some products; a Tanzanian levy on Kenyan matchboxes was reported in May 2026 despite an East African Court of Justice suspension; the 30 June 2026 NTB deadline lapsed with little progress. Bond none: pure trade interest, no kinship or grievance in the sources.
